title: Ulyana and the Cipher
premise: Insurance investigator Oscar Reyes, whose photographic memory has quietly exposed three 'accidental' deaths as murders, is handed a routine missing-persons file: Ulyana Marsh, a lighthouse keeper's daughter who vanished into the sea eleven years ago. The case should be a formality—until Oscar reads her recovered diary and realizes the entries continue for three weeks past her disappearance date. As he follows the diary's cipher through the decaying coastal town of Greywater Point, he uncovers a found family of misfits who protected Ulyana's secret, and a truth that implicates the town's beloved matriarch. In the end, Oscar must choose between exposing the whole truth and honoring the loyalty that kept five people alive—and when the tide finally gives up what it took, he closes the case with a verdict no one expected: Ulyana didn't drown; she escaped, and she's been writing to them ever since.
about_author: Petra Sandoval is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck records along the northern coast before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries from a converted boathouse, where the tide still dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Oscar Reyes, POV. Opening at a coroner's inquest where Oscar's photographic memory catches a contradiction everyone else missed—the fourth 'accident' in Greywater Point in fifteen years. He solves it quietly, as always, but the victory feels hollow. Emotional beat: isolation disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A File With No Body
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. His supervisor hands him the cold missing-persons file on Ulyana Marsh to close out an old life-insurance claim. Eleven years gone, presumed drowned. Oscar notices the file is suspiciously thin—as if someone curated it. Beat: curiosity kindling.

chapters.title: Greywater Point
chapters.summary: Oscar arrives in the fog-bound coastal town; third-person limited. He checks into the only inn, run by gruff Dez Okafor, and immediately catalogs every detail of the place. The townsfolk are polite but sealed. Beat: outsider unease.

chapters.title: The Diary
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. He receives Ulyana's recovered diary from evidence storage and begins reading. Her voice is vivid, funny, lonely—a girl who felt like a stranger even in her own family. Beat: falling for a voice from the past.

chapters.title: Three Weeks Too Many
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The central hook lands: diary entries continue nineteen days beyond her disappearance date, written in a cipher only partially decoded. Either the diary is fake—or Ulyana lived. Beat: vertigo of impossibility.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
chapters.summary: Third person, alternating Oscar and flashbacks from Ulyana's diary. Oscar interviews her father, Elias Marsh, now a broken man who tends a decommissioned light. He begs Oscar to let the dead rest. Beat: grief weaponized as a wall.

chapters.title: Five Names
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Cross-referencing the diary, Oscar identifies five recurring initials—Ulyana's secret circle of friends. He finds four still living in town: a nurse, a mechanic, a teacher, and Dez the innkeeper. Beat: the shape of a found family emerging.

chapters.title: The Cipher Key
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Working nights, he cracks the substitution cipher using his memory of the diary's repeated phrases. The hidden entries aren't about Ulyana—they're about someone else's crime, witnessed. Beat: dread replacing intrigue.

chapters.title: What Rosa Saw
chapters.summary: Rosa Ibarra, POV (the nurse). One of the circle, Rosa recognizes what Oscar is doing and confronts him at the inn. She neither confirms nor denies—but warns him that the last investigator who asked questions left town overnight. Beat: threat wrapped in kindness.

chapters.title: The Matriarch
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar meets Vivienne Ashcombe, the town's benefactor whose family owns half of Greywater Point, including the insurance company that paid out Ulyana's claim. Her charm is flawless; his memory catches one rehearsed phrase repeated verbatim across two conversations. Beat: the spider revealed.

chapters.title: Diary, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ulyana flashback chapter, first person via diary excerpts. Fifteen-year-old Ulyana describes finding something she shouldn't have at the Ashcombe estate—a ledger, a body bag, a lie. Beat: innocence colliding with corruption.

chapters.title: Someone Reads Over Your Shoulder
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. His motel room is searched; the diary copy he left behind is disturbed by millimeters only he would notice. Someone local is reporting on him. Beat: paranoia sharpening into method.

chapters.title: The Mechanic's Confession
chapters.summary: Theo Brandt, POV (the mechanic). Theo, wracked by guilt, tells Oscar a partial truth: they hid Ulyana because she begged them to, after she saw something at the Ashcombes'. Then she truly vanished—from them too. Beat: loyalty's cost made visible.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar reconstructs the timeline of the post-disappearance diary entries against tides, weather logs, and boat registrations. The entries were written somewhere reachable only at low tide. Beat: the geography of the mystery tightening.

chapters.title: The Sea Cave
chapters.summary: Third person, Oscar alone. At low tide he finds the cave beneath the old lighthouse—candles, a cot, cached food, and pages of cipher practice in Ulyana's hand. She hid here. But the last cache is empty and recent. Beat: awe curdling to fear—someone else knows.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Archive
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. A fire destroys the county records annex the night before Oscar's appointment to view the original Ashcombe ledgers. Arson, obviously. Beat: the enemy escalates; Oscar refuses to flinch.

chapters.title: Dez Breaks
chapters.summary: Dez Okafor, POV. The innkeeper admits he was Ulyana's older half-brother by a secret first marriage—her found family was blood all along. He's been protecting the circle for eleven years. Beat: betrayal reframed as devotion.

chapters.title: The Teacher's Lesson
chapters.summary: Marguerite Chen, POV (the teacher). Marguerite reveals she taught Ulyana the cipher as a game for a bullied girl who needed secrets of her own. She gives Oscar the key to the final layer of the diary. Beat: tenderness amid danger.

chapters.title: The Final Layer
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Decoded fully, the diary names what Ulyana saw: Vivienne Ashcombe's son killed a migrant dockworker and the family buried it—in the ledger, and literally. Ulyana ran because no one would believe her. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar learns why the case was 'closed': the investigating deputy was on the Ashcombe payroll, and Oscar's own company processed the payout knowing the claim was tainted. His invisibility was engineered. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: They Know Your Face Now
chapters.summary: Rosa, POV. The circle debates trusting Oscar. Rosa argues yes—not because he's safe, but because he's the first person in eleven years who could actually win. Beat: the found family votes to let him in.

chapters.title: Initiation
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. In the back room of the garage, the circle shows him their eleven years of quiet resistance—money moved, evidence duplicated, the dockworker's mother secretly supported. Oscar, orphaned and solitary, realizes he's been adopted. Beat: belonging, almost unbearable.

chapters.title: The Tide Table
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Re-reading the last diary entry, Oscar spots what everyone missed: a future date. Ulyana wrote about something that hadn't happened yet—an anniversary, this week. Either prophecy, ritual, or a promise to return. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Vivienne Invites Him to Dinner
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. A velvet-gloved summons to Ashcombe House. Vivienne offers Oscar a partnership, revealing she knows exactly who he is and what he's solved before. The threat is immaculate. Beat: charm as a blade at the throat.

chapters.title: What the Son Did
chapters.summary: Julian Ashcombe, POV. The son, now the heir, reflects on the night eleven years ago—drunk, violent, and certain his mother would fix it. She did. He narrates without remorse until the last line, where doubt creeps in. Beat: banality of evil, cracking.

chapters.title: The Mother on the Bluff
chapters.summary: Third person. Oscar visits Adaeze Nwosu, the dockworker's mother, whom the circle has quietly supported for years. She gives Oscar the one thing the Ashcombes never found: a photograph taken that night. Beat: grief as testimony.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Studying the photo, Oscar's memory cross-references it with the diary and realizes the person helping Ulyana hide wasn't any of the five friends—it was someone inside Ashcombe House. Beat: the map redraws itself.

chapters.title: The Inside Friend
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. The inside friend is revealed: Vivienne's sister, Lorna, who smuggled Ulyana supplies and then helped her disappear for real when discovery loomed. Lorna died two years ago, taking the location of her letters to the grave—almost. Beat: sacrifice honored.

chapters.title: Lorna's Letters
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Following Lorna's paper trail through probate records, Oscar finds unmailed letters in a storage unit—Ulyana alive, writing yearly, under a new name. The return address is smudged. Only one word survives: 'Ferren.' Beat: the hunt becomes a rescue.

chapters.title: Ferren
chapters.summary: Third person, Oscar traveling. A fishing village three hundred miles north. Oscar finds a woman teaching marine science to children, wearing Ulyana's ring. She sees him and says, 'You're the one with the memory. Lorna said you'd come.' Beat: the impossible made flesh.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed Gone
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV, present day. Ulyana explains: testifying would have destroyed her five protectors and freed no one—the deputy, the judge, the payout. Staying dead kept them safe. But she's been leaving the diary caches as a message in a bottle, hoping someday someone clever enough would find her. Beat: survival's guilt laid bare.

chapters.title: The Anniversary
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The date from the tide table arrives: Ulyana planned to return for the eleventh anniversary—to testify at last, whatever it cost. Oscar realizes Vivienne expects this too, and the town is being watched. Beat: countdown tension.

chapters.title: Trap at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. Ulyana comes home; Julian's men follow Oscar to the cave; the circle executes a countermove learned over eleven years of small defiance. Chaos in the dark, the sea booming below. Beat: everything converges.

chapters.title: The Fall
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Julian confronts Oscar on the bluff above the cave. In the struggle, Julian confesses aloud—knowing Oscar's memory makes the confession permanent. Julian goes over the edge into the tide. Beat: climax; horror and necessity entangled.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Third person. The storm surge uncovers remains in the sea cave—the dockworker, hidden there eleven years ago by the Ashcombes' fixer. The physical proof Ulyana always needed, delivered by the sea itself. Beat: grim vindication.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Alive, named, and sworn in, Ulyana testifies while Oscar's documented memory corroborates every detail. Vivienne, betrayed by her son's recorded confession, chooses silence over scandal and takes the fall with him. Beat: truth winning at real cost.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The legal aftermath: convictions, the insurance fraud unraveled, Oscar resigning from a company he can no longer respect. He closes Ulyana's file by hand, writing 'located, living' across the cover. Beat: professional death, personal rebirth.

chapters.title: The Sixth Chair
chapters.summary: Dez, POV. Back at the inn, the circle gathers for their first dinner in eleven years with all six seats filled—five friends and the investigator who became one. Ulyana sets a seventh plate for Lorna. Beat: found family, complete.

chapters.title: Photographs
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar, who memorizes everything but keeps nothing, allows himself one photograph: the six of them on the bluff. He realizes memory was never his burden—it was his way of refusing to let people vanish. Beat: theme resolved.

chapters.title: The Light Again
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Epilogue, one year later. The lighthouse is relit as a memorial; Ulyana is its keeper. She starts a new diary, first entry addressed to whoever finds it next. Final line: 'Some cases close. Some families open.' Beat: peace earned, door left ajar.
